# CLI Reference

<!-- Generated by `bun scripts/generate-cli-reference.ts` from the binaries' own
     help. Run it after changing a command; `bun scripts/generate-cli-reference.ts --check`
     fails when the reference has fallen behind the code. -->

Every command below is one the binary actually has. The exit codes are the ones
the `E`-code scheme in the [README](../README.md#error-codes) describes: `0` is
success, `2` is a validation failure, `3` a configuration failure, `4` a git
failure, `5` a security failure, `124` a timeout and `127` a command that is not
installed.

## fs-app

The cross-platform app tool: hooks, builds, simulators and emulators.

```
Git hooks and development tools for Foodshare iOS

Usage: fs-app [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  format       Format Swift code with enterprise-grade safety features
  lint         Lint Swift code
  commit-msg   Validate commit message
  secrets      Scan for secrets
  migrations   Check migrations status
  build        Build project
  test         Run tests
  run          Build, install, and run the app on simulator
  simulator    List simulators
  doctor       Diagnose environment
  project      Xcode project management
  verify       Verify setup
  pre-push     Pre-push checks - validates build, lint, and tests before push
  deps         Manage Swift package dependencies
  protect      Code protection system - snapshots, recovery, and safety guards
  emulator     Manage Android emulators
  swift-build  Build Swift for Android
  swift-java   Generate Swift-Java bindings
  swift-core   Build FoodshareCore Swift library for Android
  supabase     Supabase backend operations
  help         Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -c, --config <CONFIG>  Config file path
  -v, --verbose...       Increase output verbosity
  -q, --quiet            Suppress non-error output
      --no-color         Disable colored output
  -h, --help             Print help
  -V, --version          Print version
```

### fs-app format

```
Format Swift code with enterprise-grade safety features

Usage: fs-app format [OPTIONS] [FILES]...

Arguments:
  [FILES]...  Files to format

Options:
  -c, --config <CONFIG>  Config file path
      --check            Check only, don't modify (legacy flag, use --preview)
      --staged           Format only staged files
  -v, --verbose...       Increase output verbosity
      --preview          Preview mode: show what would change without modifying files
  -q, --quiet            Suppress non-error output
      --lang <LANG>      Language: ios, android, both [default: ios]
      --no-color         Disable colored output
      --backup           Create a stash backup before formatting (default: true)
      --no-backup        Disable backup (equivalent to --backup=false)
      --show-diff        Show detailed diff of changes
      --audit            Enable audit logging
      --snapshot         Create a snapshot before formatting (Code Protection System, default: true)
      --no-snapshot      Disable snapshot creation
  -h, --help             Print help
```

### fs-app pre-push

```
Pre-push checks - validates build, lint, and tests before push

Usage: fs-app pre-push [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -c, --config <CONFIG>        Config file path
      --fail-fast <FAIL_FAST>  Fail fast on first error (defaults to the configuration) [possible
                               values: true, false]
      --release <RELEASE>      Use release build for validation (defaults to the configuration)
                               [possible values: true, false]
  -v, --verbose...             Increase output verbosity
  -q, --quiet                  Suppress non-error output
      --quick                  Quick mode: skip optional checks (tests)
      --no-color               Disable colored output
      --skip <SKIP>            Skip specific checks (comma-separated: lint,build,test)
      --detailed               Show detailed output for pre-push checks
  -h, --help                   Print help
```

## foodshare-i18n

The translation tool: health, audits, translations and deployment.

```
Enterprise-grade translation management CLI for Foodshare

Usage: foodshare-i18n [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  health              Check system health and status
  test                Test translation system
  audit               Audit translation coverage
  translate           Auto-translate missing keys
  bench               Benchmark translation endpoints
  locales             List supported locales
  deploy              Deploy translation system
  update              Update translations
  backfill            Backfill translations for existing posts
  generate-infoplist  Generate localized InfoPlist.strings files for iOS
  help                Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -v, --verbose          Enable verbose output
  -f, --format <FORMAT>  Output format (text, json) [default: text]
  -h, --help             Print help
  -V, --version          Print version
```

## fs-image

The image tool: detect, analyse, resize and strip alpha.

```
Image processing and optimization CLI

Usage: fs-image <COMMAND>

Commands:
  detect        Detect image format from file
  metadata      Extract metadata from image
  analyze       Analyze images in a directory
  recommend     Calculate recommended resize for image
  remove-alpha  Remove alpha channel from images
  resize        Resize images to specific dimensions
  help          Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

  -V, --version  Print version
```

### fs-image remove-alpha

```
Remove alpha channel from images

Usage: fs-image remove-alpha [OPTIONS] <PATH>

Arguments:
  <PATH>  Path to image file or directory

Options:
      --background <BACKGROUND>
          Background color in hex format (e.g., ffffff for white) [default: ffffff]
      --overwrite
          Overwrite original files
  -o, --output <OUTPUT>
          Output directory (if not overwriting)
  -r, --recursive
          Process directory recursively
      --dry-run
          Dry run - show what would be processed without making changes
      --filter-dimensions <FILTER_DIMENSIONS>
          Only process images with specific dimensions (e.g., "1284x2778" for iPhone 6.9")
  -h, --help
          Print help
```

### fs-image resize

```
Resize images to specific dimensions

Usage: fs-image resize [OPTIONS] --output <OUTPUT> <PATH>

Arguments:
  <PATH>  Path to image file or directory

Options:
  -w, --width <WIDTH>      Target width in pixels
```
